question: Should OpenClaw define an agent-origin attestation trust contract, and which outbound paths, signing authority, verifier trust root, and privacy properties should that contract cover?
rationale: Code inspection proves the capability is absent, but it cannot choose what an OpenClaw signature should assert or safely settle identity stability, key custody, replay defense, redirect behavior, and path coverage.

options.title: Design a generic attestation seam
options.body: Define a threat-modeled, opt-in domain/audience-scoped signing API and let plugins or service integrations supply policy through that generic contract.

options.title: Keep identity service-specific
options.body: Decline an OpenClaw-wide identity claim and require ordinary credentials or service-specific challenge/response implemented by each plugin or backend.

options.title: Offer attribution without attestation
options.body: Permit non-cryptographic product/version headers on narrowly approved paths while explicitly documenting that they do not prove an agent originated the request.

recommendation.title: Design a generic attestation seam
recommendation.body: Define a threat-modeled, opt-in domain/audience-scoped signing API and let plugins or service integrations supply policy through that generic contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest available product/security and adjacent implementation provenance, including the existing keep-open decision.
